result.title: GGDriver: Glance at What Is Shared, Gaze at What Differs for Perception-Free Planning
result.summary: A planner deciding whether to turn left or continue straight needs to inspect different parts of the scene for each maneuver. Yet many end-to-end driving planners evaluate every candidate trajectory against the same compressed scene representation. We let each candidate select the visual evidence used to refine and score it. A global glance first produces trajectory hypotheses from shared scene features. We then project a corridor around each trajectory into the camera views and use the resulting mask to attend to patch features at the backbone's native resolution. After refinement, the scorer projects each final proposal again and ranks it using evidence along its own path. This geometric selection requires only the predicted trajectory and camera calibration. On three planners with different scene representations (learned registers, a perception-supervised bird's-eye-view grid, and a coarse image-token grid), adding this gaze improves planning scores. In ablations, path-aligned patches outperform both a matched number of randomly selected patches and attention over all patches. Using the gaze for ranking yields larger gains than using it for refinement alone. With a ViT-S backbone and no perception labels, GGDriver achieves a rater feedback score of 8.110 on the WOD-E2E test set, 94.2 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1, 48.6 EPDMS on NAVSIM-v2, and a closed-loop Driving Score of 72.18 on Bench2Drive.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GGDriver：先用共享场景特征生成轨迹假设，再把每条候选轨迹周围的走廊投影到相机视图，按掩码在原分辨率的 patch 特征上取路径对齐证据，分别用于轨迹精化与最终打分排序，并在三种场景表示与消融中比较效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 按候选假设定向筛选视觉证据、并分别用于精化与打分的做法，与 LVR 中「生成内容是否真正使用视觉证据」及证据贡献分配问题相通；其掩码注意与「路径对齐 vs 随机/全patch」消融可供核查借鉴，但任务是自动驾驶规划而非语言推理。
